rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Pair production requires a nucleus to conserve momentum — a photon alone cannot produce a particle-antiparticle pair even if it has enough energy, because momentum conservation would be violated if the particles are at rest.  ·  Fusion does NOT occur in ordinary stars like the Sun because the 'fusion' of everyday materials involves atomic (electron) interactions, not nuclear. Fusion requires overcoming the Coulomb barrier at 10⁷-10⁸ K, far hotter than any chemical reaction.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Nuclear fission is NOT the same as radioactive decay. Fission requires a neutron to trigger the split; decay is spontaneous. Fission releases ∼200 MeV; decay releases typically 1-5 MeV.  ·  The energy in nuclear reactions comes from the binding energy difference (mass defect), NOT from the rest mass of the fuel itself being 'converted.' Only Δm (the mass difference between reactants and products) converts, not the entire fuel mass.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Einstein's E = mc² is a special case of the full equation E² = (mc²)² + (pc)², which applies to moving particles. At rest (p=0), this reduces to E = mc².  ·  The binding energy curve peaks at iron-56. This is why stars stop producing energy via fusion once they form iron — fusing iron consumes energy instead of releasing it, which is the trigger for stellar collapse and supernova.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: **Particle creation (pair production):** A high-energy photon (γ-ray) with energy hν ≥ 2mc² can create a particle-antiparticle pair. For electron-positron: γ → e⁺ + e⁻. The minimum photon energy is 2m_e c² = 1.022 MeV. Both rest mass energy (2mc²) and momentum must be conserved, requiring a nearby nucleus to absorb recoil.  ·  **Pair production threshold:** For a photon to create a particle of mass m at rest, the photon must have energy at least E_min = 2mc² (for pair production). In the center-of-mass frame, the threshold is exactly 2mc². At rest, the created particles have zero kinetic energy.  ·  **Annihilation:** When a particle meets its antiparticle, they annihilate, converting their entire rest mass into energy. e⁺ + e⁻ → γ + γ (two photons to conserve momentum). Total energy released = 2m_e c² = 1.022 MeV.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Nuclear fusion and fission are NOT just 'bigger bombs' — fusion is the opposite of fission in terms of the binding energy curve. Fusion moves nuclei toward the peak (iron); fission moves heavy nuclei toward the peak too. Both release energy by moving toward greater stability.  ·  Note 3: Practice numerical problems regularly for mastery of Creation and annihilation; nuclear fission and fusion  ·  Note 4: Remember the units and dimensions involved in Creation and annihilation; nuclear fission and fusion
